problem:
Given that the differential equation 

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+2x{y}^{′}-12y=2{x}^{2}+1,\,x>0
$$

has the complimentary function ${y}_{c}(x)=A{x}^{3}+\frac{B}{{x}^{4}}$, find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ to this equation.
worked_solution:
The right-hand side of the inhomogeneous equation is  $2{x}^{2}+1.$ Therefore, we assume that the particular solution is of the form 

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=\alpha {x}^{2}+\beta ,
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are the constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x}=2\alpha x,\,\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}=2\alpha .
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation and group the terms on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}(2\alpha )+2x(2\alpha x)-12(\alpha {x}^{2}+\beta ) & =2{x}^{2}+1 \\ (2\alpha +4\alpha -12\alpha ){x}^{2}-12\beta  & =2{x}^{2}+1 \\ -6\alpha {x}^{2}-12\beta  & =2{x}^{2}+1\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-6\alpha =2\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\,{x}^{2}) \\ -12\beta =1\, & (\text{equating the constants})\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =-\frac{1}{3},\,\,\beta =-\frac{1}{12}.$

Hence, the particular integral ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=-\frac{{x}^{2}}{3}-\frac{1}{12}.
$$
